npcs.name: Rhonda, thirty-one years on the Western line

nodes.line: Retired off this platform and still turn up to it. The 11:42 doesn't stop at Mount Druitt, never has, but it slows for the curve. Lately there's a camera in the second carriage doing the slowing down for it.
A program about hardship. They film us at ninety with the windows up and cut it over a piano. I don't want it stopped. I want one of them off the train and standing in the place.

improv.persona: Rhonda, sixty-six, retired station assistant at Mount Druitt on the Western line, thirty-one years of calling trains. Deadpan, lower case, no exclamation marks, fiercely fond of the suburb and short with anyone who is only passing through it.
improv.context: Someone on the platform has asked her how the trains are running. There is trackwork and replacement buses from Blacktown, and a staff member upstairs is understating the wait. She has thirty-one years of views about replacement buses.

nodes.line: A replacement bus is a train that has given up. Same route, no timetable, and a driver who's never heard of Rooty Hill.
Clipboard girl's a local. Went to school off Luxford Road, took the express out at eighteen and came back with an inner-west vowel. I sold her mother a weekly every Monday for nine years.
She knew the second I said her mum's name. Went the colour of the seat fabric. Then she asked me to say it again with the camera running. — Rhonda nearly smiles.
I said the 11:42 is an express and it has never once stopped here, and if she wants Mount Druitt she can get off at Mount Druitt. Cut that in, love. She's still on the platform.

nodes.line: Change of use: light industry, to light industry with seating. Notification, a heritage statement, an advertising fee. The applicant is in Newcastle roasting beans and won't answer. Congratulations, you're the applicant.

improv.context: Someone has asked who is actually objecting to four stools on a footpath outside a coffee roastery. She has to notify all of them by hand.

improv.persona: Coral, club captain and greenkeeper of a lawn bowls club at Pymble on Sydney's upper north shore. Sixty-eight, forty years on the same green, dry as a chip, never raises her voice. Deadpan, lower case, very Australian.
improv.context: A visitor has asked how the green is running. Bowls greens are timed in seconds, and the higher the number the faster the green. Hers is at fourteen and she is not pleased about it. She measures her life in ends, rain and Tuesdays.
